title: The Hills Have Eyes II
full_review:
In last year's remake of Wes Craven's 1977 horror film, the Carter family fell prey to mutants on a secret military base in New Mexico. A few government scientists and members of a National Guard unit are the ones doomed in "The Hills Have Eyes II" (Fox), an equally repellant sequel that doesn't hold back on the gruesome violence.

At least the soldiers' weapons give them a fighting chance; the Carters had none. As before, audience members can shut their eyes or wave a white flag of surrender at the projectionist.

The group of nine inexperienced soldiers gets whittled down to three (Michael McMillian, Jessica Stroup and Daniella Alonso) and the mutants only spare the two women so they can preserve their cannibalistic race and continue to dwell in an abandoned, radioactive mine.

Putting a band of soldiers into the horror cross hairs turns this exercise into a recognizable game of survival. Having them training for deployment in Iraq adds a topical note. But early stabs at providing commentary on the attitude and preparedness of the nation's armed forces prove less than trenchant.

Morocco stands in for the desert Southwest and director Martin Weisz does a decent job of incorporating the landscape. Once the action moves underground and out of the sunlight, he really cranks up the gore factor. Still, hardly anything could be more disturbing than the movie's opening scene in which a captive woman gives birth to a half-mutant child.

The film contains excessive graphic violence, including bloody dismemberment, numerous impalings and shootings, a suicide, a rape, upper female nudity, pervasive rough and crude language, and some profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
